documents.title: Obstetric Discharge Summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
LABOR AND DELIVERY - REGIONAL HOSPITAL
Discharge Summary
Admission 2025-06-15 / Discharge 2025-06-17

29 y/o G2P1001 at 39w2d (EDD 2025-06-20).

Diagnoses: intrauterine pregnancy at term, delivered. Active phase arrest (working diagnosis at 4 cm after 6 hours of oxytocin). Vaginal delivery.
History: mild intermittent asthma, albuterol as needed. Prior delivery 2024-06-19, vaginal, after oxytocin augmentation for slow active-phase progress. Prenatal care this pregnancy uncomplicated; prenatal labs unremarkable.

Course: Came in roughly a year after her first delivery, contracting every 3 minutes, cervix 4 cm on arrival. Epidural placed. Oxytocin started for augmentation. After 6 hours on oxytocin her exam was unchanged: 4 cm, 80% effaced, vertex at -2, with strong contractions coming every 2-3 minutes. An intrauterine pressure catheter showed an average of 220 Montevideo units over 10 minutes. The fetal heart rate pattern was reassuring throughout on continuous monitoring, with no decelerations. She was afebrile with stable vital signs.

Because she had not yet reached 6 cm, the team judged her still in latent labor by current criteria and continued oxytocin with amniotomy rather than proceed to cesarean. She subsequently made cervical change, reached complete dilation and delivered vaginally a liveborn infant. Uncomplicated third stage.

Postpartum: routine. Discharged home postpartum day 2 in good condition.
Allergies: NKDA.
Home meds at discharge: albuterol inhaler as needed.
Follow-up: OB office 6 weeks.

Dictated by obstetrics hospitalist.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam. 29 y/o, second baby born 6/15 by vaginal delivery at the outside hospital - this labor stalled at 4 cm despite oxytocin, they kept going rather than section and she delivered. Discharge summary reviewed. OB postpartum visit is next week.

Doing well. Two under 14 months, so 'tired' is the word. Off for the summer. PHQ-9 2. Sleep is the main thing.

Asthma - hasn't touched the inhaler since winter. No cough.

No meds besides albuterol prn. NKDA. Never smoker, no EtOH.

Exam: BP and vitals per flowsheet. Comfortable. Neck without masses. Lungs clear, no wheeze. RRR, no murmur. Abd soft, nontender, no masses. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix normal-appearing, Pap collected. Ext without edema. Affect bright.

A/P
1. Preventive - Pap today (last 2022 normal). Labs not needed this year, normal CBC last August. Flu and COVID vaccines in the fall.
2. Mild intermittent asthma - stable, no change.
3. Postpartum mood - fine. She knows to message if that changes.

See in a year.

documents.title: Surprise
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Well, this is a surprise for everyone. Home test positive yesterday. I haven't really had a normal period since the baby so I don't know my dates - I think maybe mid July. OB is getting me in for an ultrasound next week. Wanted you to know. First day of school is Wednesday, so that's fun.

documents.title: RE: Surprise
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for letting me know, and congratulations. The ultrasound will sort out the dates. Same as before - albuterol is fine if you need it, and flu/COVID shots are recommended this fall. Good luck with the first week.

OUTSIDE OBSTETRICS AND GYNECOLOGY GROUP - new OB visit 2025-09-15

29 y/o G3P2002. LMP uncertain postpartum; patient's recollection about 2025-07-12. Transvaginal ultrasound 2025-09-02: single IUP, CRL consistent with 7w3d, cardiac activity present. Dated by ultrasound; EDD 2026-04-18.

OB history:
- 2024-06-19 SVD at 39w1d, oxytocin augmentation, arrest of active-phase dilation that responded to augmentation
- 2025-06-15 vaginal delivery at 39w2d, labeled active phase arrest at 4 cm, delivered after continued oxytocin
Short interval from the last delivery to this conception, about 6 weeks.

Med hx: mild intermittent asthma, albuterol prn. NKDA. No surgeries.

Prenatal labs collected; unremarkable.

Plan: routine prenatal care.
- Obstetrics attending
